messages:
Samir (Sales Eng): Hey team — Customer 'Orion Health' wants a Private deployment for their POC. Main asks: preserve client source IP for downstream auth, prefer PrivateLink if possible, and a strict firewall allowlist. Any immediate blockers on our side?
Nadia (Network Eng): PrivateLink is doable. Preserving client src IP depends on where the traffic terminates. If they route through our proxy/edge, we do NAT; if they terminate directly into customer-managed VPC via interface endpoint, src IP can be preserved. Need to confirm their topology.
Maya (AE): They said they'd prefer interface endpoints + their own NLB in front of the connector. They also flagged that any NAT/EIP substitution will break their SAML rules.
Devin (SRE): If we're asked to run a connector in their VPC (Private deployment), we can avoid NAT by using host networking and mapping 443 directly. But our docs assume an outbound egress to our control plane for metrics — that part needs allowlist.
Samir (Sales Eng): Great. Can you list exact IPs/ports they'd need to allow? Also call out whether PrivateLink vs VPC Peering has cost or SLA implications for billing the POC.
Nadia (Network Eng): Minimal list for POC: 443/TCP outbound to control-plane endpoints (by FQDN); 53/UDP if they rely on our DNS bridge; 123/UDP if they need NTP. For PrivateLink (interface endpoint) we rely on AWS-managed addresses — customer will see ENIs in their VPC. No cross-account NAT needed. For peering you'd have route table changes and potential transitive routing blockers.
Devin (SRE): Control-plane FQDNs: control.redwood-inference.net and metrics.redwood-inference.net (we prefer FQDN allowlist + TLS). If they insist on IPs, we can provide a peering-list but it's dynamic — recommend FQDN + TLS validation.
Samir (Sales Eng): Customer asked about egress bandwidth pricing for the Dedicated/private deploy vs hosted. Any quick guidance?
Maya (AE): Pricing: Private deployments are licensed (platform + support). Data transfer costs depend on where their VPC lives; e.g., inter-AZ traffic is free, inter-region is chargeable. We should run a rough estimate off their expected RPS and average output token size. Can Solutions Eng help with a ballpark?
Devin (SRE): For POC we can cap throughput and enable sampling. Also recommend quantization/CPU fallbacks for cost control. But network egress to our S3/metrics (if used) may incur standard cloud data transfer fees.
Nadia (Network Eng): Security Qs: They asked about Firewall rules for PrivateLink endpoint policy. Suggest starting with: Allow TCP 443 to interface endpoint IPs (or allow the endpoint FQDN), deny 0.0.0.0/0 outbound, and restrict SG inbound to their mgmt CIDR. Add TLS mutual auth if they want mTLS — we support customer mTLS cert upload for the connector.
Samir (Sales Eng): They also sent a quick security questionnaire item: 'Can Redwood guarantee no egress to third-party IPs?' — how do we respond?
Nadia (Network Eng): Short answer: We route only to configured control-plane FQDNs and customer-configured destinations. We don't route customer model data to third-party analytics by default. For a binding answer, we need to propose an architecture and include it in the SOC/contractual docs.
Maya (AE): Customer also requested an architecture diagram and a one-page checklist for their firewall team. Can someone draft and I'll attach to the SQA?
Devin (SRE): I'll spin up a simple checklist: required FQDNs, ports, example SG rules, and a note about IPs vs FQDNs. Nadia — can you add the PrivateLink vs Peering pros/cons slide?
Nadia (Network Eng): Yep. Quick pros/cons: PrivateLink — no route table changes, better isolation, ENIs in customer account, easier for restrictive security posture. Peering — lower latency for intra-VPC traffic, but requires route changes and careful CIDR planning; transitive routing often not allowed.
Samir (Sales Eng): Perfect. Last ask: any enterprise blockers that might delay the POC sign-off?
Devin (SRE): Potential blocker: customer requires on-premairgapped deployment for initial eval. We can offer an on-prem package but it needs additional legal, security, and infra prep — 2-4 week lead. Otherwise PrivateLink POC should be ~5 business days to stand up if customer teams move quickly.
Maya (AE): I'll tell them the PrivateLink timeline and the on-prem lead time. Samir — can you confirm the POC acceptance criteria (latency SLO, token throughput) so we can size nodes?
Samir (Sales Eng): Will do. I'll share a small questionnaire back to them and ask for expected RPS, average prompt/response token count, and whether they need src-ip preservation end-to-end.
deploy-bot: Scheduled: send checklist draft to #sales in 2h per request by @Devin (SRE). :robot_face: 
Samir (Sales Eng): Thanks everyone — looping in the customer now. I'll paste the checklist link when they respond. :thumbsup:
